To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have excluded the existence of SIMPs and nuclearites with masses in the 10-10(3) GeV range.
we have set new limits on SIMPs and nuclearites, and that we have shown that our data are in good agreement with the Standard Model.
The DAMA/LIBRA–NaI(Tl) experiment excludes the existence of neutral strongly interacting massive particle candidates (SIMPs) in the mass range 1–1000 GeV/c(2), at a 90% confidence level.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development and testing of a novel, high-performance, low-cost, low-power, low-maintenance, high-availability, high-reliability and secure networked computing infrastructure, which can support large-scale distributed applications in Grid environments.
the development and testing of new technologies for the detection of rare events.
the search for WIMP-like interactions in a low-energy regime, with a sensitivity to low mass WIMPs, down to the keV range.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
no evidence has been found in favor of the existence of SIMPs or nuclearites, and that the present results represent the most stringent limits to date.
the DAMA annual modulation effect has been clearly demonstrated by the model-independent and model-dependent results of the experiment and that it cannot be ascribed to any known systematic effect.
no evidence for the presence of neutral massive stable SIMPs or nuclearites in the 1-10 GeV/c(2) mass region has been obtained.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we can exclude SIMPs of mass M = (1-50) GeV/c(2) at a confidence level of 90% and 99%, respectively, for cross section sigma-nucleon > similar or equal to (1-2) x 10(-6) pb.
the DAMA/LIBRA and NaI(Tl)-phase1 data, as well as the DAMA/NaI-annual modulation data, are compatible with the existence of a dark matter candidate, which is not a WIMP.

we have excluded the SIMP interpretation for the DAMA annual modulation signal at 99% CL for the SIMP mass in the range 0.5-0.7 GeV, and for the SIMP-nucleon scattering cross section in the range 10(-41) - 10(-39) cm2.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the DAMA experiment has the potential to exclude a significant portion of the parameter space for the SIMP dark matter model.
we have improved the limits on the mass and the cross section by an order of magnitude.
we have improved the exclusion plots for the SIMP parameter space by a factor of 2-3.
